source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / Directorate General of Agriculture, "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកសៀង" [Soybean cultivation techniques], official extension manual, 2018
text: Cambodia-specific background: the manual states soybean has been grown in Cambodia since the 1950s, historically concentrated in Kampong Cham province and along the Mekong river's flood-recession (ដីល្បោះ / colmatage-type) soils and adjoining upland red soil, later expanding to other provinces. It gives a 3-year national statistics table (2014–2016 area, production, and yield) with area falling from roughly 66,160 ha (2014) to roughly 47,947 ha (2016) while total production likewise declined, and average yield reported as increasing modestly year over year (roughly 1.46, 1.66, then 1.75 t/ha across the three years cited) — illustrated with bar charts pairing area and yield per year.
